title: Proteins and Protein Synthesis
text: Proteins are large biomolecules consisting of chains of amino acids and are essential for virtually all biological processes. The sequence of amino acids in a protein is determined by the nucleotide sequence of the gene encoding it. Protein synthesis occurs in two stages: transcription, in which DNA is copied into messenger RNA (mRNA), and translation, in which the mRNA is decoded by ribosomes to produce a polypeptide chain. Proteins fold into specific three-dimensional structures that determine their function. They serve as enzymes, structural components (such as collagen and keratin), signaling molecules (hormones), and antibodies.
